body.text: ERPNext for construction companies brings budgets, progress billing, retention, subcontractors, site stock and labour costs into one system, so contractors can see profit on every project before the final invoice. Teknoppy sets it up for civil, MEP, fit-out and infrastructure contractors across Kerala, India and the GCC.

paragraphs.text: Yes. ERPNext links every purchase, timesheet, subcontractor bill and client invoice to a project, so cost and revenue build up as work happens. Budgets come from your bill of quantities, progress bills follow your measurements, and retention is tracked on both sides. Setting up ERPNext for construction companies usually takes 10–14 weeks for a contractor with several live projects.

ERPNext for contracting companies replaces the mix of spreadsheets, site registers and accounting software that most contractors rely on. As ERPNext construction software, it has no licence fee per user, so site engineers, storekeepers and project managers can all log in without extra cost.

sections.h2: Signs Your Projects Need a Better System

items.text: Project profit is only known after the final account
Site stores and head office disagree on material balances
Running bills take more than a week to prepare
Nobody can say quickly how much retention is owed to you
Subcontractor bills are approved without checking measured work

outro.text: If three or more apply, ERPNext for construction companies usually pays for itself through tighter cost control and faster billing within the first year.

paragraphs.text: ERPNext project costing shows actual cost against budget for every project, broken down by material, labour, subcontract, equipment and overheads. When a purchase order or timesheet is approved, the cost lands on the project straight away, not at month-end.

ERPNext BOQ management turns your bill of quantities into budget lines, so each item has a target cost and quantity. ERPNext job costing construction reports then show margin per project, per BOQ item and per phase. Owners finally see which projects make money while there is still time to act.

rows: Cost per BOQ item against its budget
Billed revenue minus all costs to date
Remaining budget and expected final cost
Purchase orders and subcontracts not yet billed

paragraphs.text: ERPNext progress billing creates running bills from measured quantities or percentage complete, with the previous billed amount, this period's work and the cumulative total. Advance payments are recovered automatically from each bill, and ERPNext retention money is deducted and tracked until it is released at handover or after the defects period.

Retention works both ways. ERPNext tracks what your client holds back from you and what you hold back from subcontractors, so you always know what is due, from whom and when. ERPNext contract billing also handles variation orders, so approved changes are added to the contract value and billed correctly.

Contractors often receive mobilisation advances, give performance and advance-payment guarantees, and wait months for retention. ERPNext records each advance and recovers it from running bills, tracks guarantee amounts and expiry dates, and lists expected receipts by project. Finance teams see how much cash is tied up in retention and unbilled work, which helps plan the next tender. Any partner setting up ERPNext for construction companies should include this view, because cash, not profit, is what usually stops a growing contractor.

ERPNext subcontractor billing records each subcontract with its scope, rates and retention. Subcontractor bills are checked against measured work before approval, so you never pay for work that has not been done. Back-charges for materials supplied, damage or delays are deducted on the same bill, with the reason recorded for any later dispute.

paragraphs.html: ERPNext timesheets construction setups capture labour hours by project and activity, from site supervisors on mobile or from biometric devices. Labour cost then flows to each project at the correct rate, including overtime. For contractors with large workforces in the Gulf, payroll and WPS can run in the same system; see ERPNext HR and payroll for the GCC.

paragraphs.text: ERPNext material management construction setups give each site its own store. Materials are issued against the project and activity, transfers between sites are recorded, and unused stock is returned. Storekeepers can work from a tablet, and managers see what is on each site without a phone call. Material requests from site go to purchasing with the project and BOQ item attached, so buyers know exactly what the order is for and which budget it uses.

Owned and hired equipment is tracked by project, with usage hours charged to each job. Fuel, operator costs and repairs are booked against the machine and the project it was working on, so you know the true cost of every crane, excavator and generator. Maintenance schedules and hire agreements keep machines working and costs visible. ERPNext site management brings materials, equipment and labour together for each location.

ERPNext project management construction setups break each project into phases and tasks, with planned dates, owners and progress. Site engineers update progress on mobile, and the same progress feeds billing and cost-to-complete reports. ERPNext construction management therefore links what is happening on site with what is happening in the accounts.

outro.text: As an ERPNext construction consultant, we combine project controls with ERPNext construction accounting, so the site and the office use the same numbers. That is what makes ERPNext for construction companies worth the change.

paragraphs.text: Contractors in Ernakulam and across the state use our ERPNext construction Kochi team, with workshops at our Vyttila office. We provide ERPNext construction Kerala-wide for building, civil and interior contractors.
Our ERPNext construction India setups include GST on works contracts, TDS on contractor payments and e-way bills for material moves.

items.q: Does it work on site from mobile?
items.a: Yes. Site engineers can update progress and timesheets, and storekeepers can issue materials, from phones or tablets. Managers see the updates immediately.
Yes. Each subcontract is recorded with its scope, rates and retention, and subcontractor bills are checked against measured work before approval.

items.q: How long does setup take for a contractor?
items.a: A contractor with a handful of live projects usually goes live in 10–14 weeks. Larger groups with many sites take 14–20 weeks. We start with one or two projects to keep billing safe.

items.q: What does ERPNext cost for a contractor?
items.a: The price depends on the number of live projects, sites, users and how detailed your BOQs are. ERPNext itself has no licence fee. A partner setting up ERPNext for construction companies should send a phased, fixed quote after a short discovery call, and ours lists every line item.

items.q: Is ERPNext suitable for small contractors?
items.a: Yes. ERPNext for contractors has no licence fee per user, so small firms can start with project costing and billing, then add site stores and payroll later.
